pages.title: Overview
pages.body:
LANGUAGE is built as brutalist architecture: six glyph masses of shared box strokes standing on plinths, split by a walkable plaza. A raking dawn sun reads the word through its own shadows. The camera runs one 132-second loop: high and far so the word is legible as language, then down into the ruin and through the plaza.

Navigate through the pages below to walk through each section of this file.

pages.title: Letterforms as stone
pages.body: Each glyph is a list of rectangles on a 5×7 grid. Diagonals are stepped, not sloped, because every stroke, plinth, column, and rubble block is a scaled instance of one unit BoxGeometry. Nothing is allocated per glyph or per frame.

pages.title: Setup — site, sun, first frame
pages.body: setup() calls setHelp first, then stages haze fog, a dawn sky dome, a shadow-receiving ground, the monument group, colonnades culled off the camera path, and a low directional sun with a cool fill. placeCamera(ctx, 0) poses the opening reading view before update() ever runs.

pages.title: Update — two-act camera
pages.body: update() only moves the camera along the closed loop. No geometry is created or mutated per frame.

pages.title: Teardown
pages.body: teardown() removes every root, disposes shared geometries, materials, textures, and light shadow maps, and restores the prior fog, background, and orbit controls.
